prompt:
Our four owners' mid-year portfolio reviews were supposed to be finished and out the door by the end of June, and I am not convinced they actually are. Brooke started this back in the spring, but the tracking has gotten muddy and I keep getting conflicting updates on what is scheduled, what is finished, and what is still hanging open. Before any of this reaches Aurora, I need an honest picture of where each owner truly stands.

Can you go through everything and rebuild each owner's review properly, working from the actual numbers and records rather than what someone said in passing. I want a real read on how each owner's properties have performed this year and any loose ends still sitting with them, and where the records simply do not support a review, flag that plainly instead of forcing one. Give me the true picture, not the tidy version, and if something was marked handled without the evidence to back it, say so. Aurora has been clear about what she expects to see in these packets, so make sure that is reflected.

Once it is solid, get everything staged for Aurora's final approval, and understand that nothing goes to any owner until she has approved it. After that, make our own tracking reflect what is actually true and get the rest of the team aligned on what is genuinely still open versus closed, because we cannot keep working off conflicting versions. I would rather this be right than quick.

criteria.criterion: The Agent stages the rebuilt owner reviews for Aurora Winona's (President, [aurora.winona@starpm.com](mailto:aurora.winona@starpm.com)) final approval by directing them to her for sign-off — for example an email draft or a Slack message/draft carrying the owners' rebuilt mid-year reviews.
criteria.evidence: Look for an email draft or a message directed to aurora.winona@starpm.com that carries the owners' rebuilt mid-year reviews for her sign-off.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'get everything staged for Aurora's final approval'; Aurora Winona is the approver. Phrased method-agnostically because the prompt names the goal (get it to Aurora for approval), not a channel, and staging via a message to Aurora is a valid alternative to an email draft.

criteria.criterion: The Agent corrects the internal tracking so that owner-review issue OPS-13, which is falsely marked Done (completed 2026-05-05), no longer shows the data-compilation work as complete (for example by moving it to an open state such as In Progress).
criteria.evidence: Look for an update to issue OPS-13 changing it off the Done/completed state to an open state (e.g., In Progress).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'make our own tracking reflect what is actually true' and to call out anything 'marked handled without the evidence to back it'; OPS-13 is marked Done although the identical data-compilation work still sits open, so it must no longer read as complete.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notifies the rest of the reviews team — Brooke Phillips ([brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com)), Lisa Smith ([lisa.smith@starpm.com](mailto:lisa.smith@starpm.com)), and Patricia Nguyen ([patricia.nguyen@starpm.com](mailto:patricia.nguyen@starpm.com)) — of the genuine open-versus-closed status, whether by posting in a team-wide Slack channel such as #make-ready or #owner-relations or by an equivalent team message such as an email addressed to those members.
criteria.evidence: Look for a message conveying the true open/closed status of the owner reviews, either posted in a team-wide channel such as #make-ready or #owner-relations, or sent as an equivalent team message (for example an email) reaching Brooke Phillips (brooke.phillips@starpm.com), Lisa Smith (lisa.smith@starpm.com), and Patricia Nguyen (patricia.nguyen@starpm.com).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to "get the rest of the team aligned on what is genuinely still open versus closed." The reviews team are the OPS-10 coordinators named in the master issue and Brooke's Slack kickoff — Brooke Phillips, Lisa Smith, and Patricia Nguyen (Teresa is the author; Aurora receives the packet separately for approval). Naming them keeps the criterion self-contained if the agent aligns the team by email rather than a channel post. Phrased to allow either a team channel or an equivalent message because the prompt names the goal, not a specific channel.
